questions.prompt: With the bias current held fixed and \(R_D \ll r_o\), you double \(R_D\) (the device stays saturated). What happens to the gain?
options: It is unchanged, since \(g_m\) is unchanged
questions.explanation: \(A_v = -g_m(r_o\parallel R_D) \approx -g_mR_D\). The catch is headroom: the DC drop \(I_DR_D\) doubles too.

questions.explanation: \(|A_v| \to g_mr_o = 120\), the intrinsic gain. Any finite load only lowers it.

options: \(|A_v| = 2V_{RD}/V_{ov}\), where \(V_{RD} = I_DR_D\) is the DC drop across \(R_D\)
questions.explanation: \(g_m = 2I_D/V_{ov}\), so \(g_mR_D = 2I_DR_D/V_{ov}\). More gain needs a bigger DC drop or a smaller overdrive.

questions.prompt: A CS stage (\(g_m = 2\ \mathrm{mS}\), \(R_D = 5\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\), \(r_o\) ignored) is driven by a source with \(R_{sig} = 50\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\). Find \(v_{out}/v_{sig}\) at low frequency.
questions.explanation: The gate draws no current, so no signal is lost across \(R_{sig}\): \(A_v = -g_mR_D = -10\). Dividing by \(R_{sig}\) assumes a finite input resistance. (At high frequency \(R_{sig}\) does matter.)

questions.prompt: Preview of high-impedance loads: at \(V_{ov} = 0.2\ \mathrm{V}\), a resistor-loaded CS stage needs what DC drop across \(R_D\) for a gain of 100?
options: 10 V, impractical on a low-voltage supply, so a current-source load is used
questions.explanation: \(V_{RD} = |A_v|V_{ov}/2 = 10\ \mathrm{V}\). A current source gives a large small-signal resistance with a small DC drop.

questions.explanation: \((-10)(-10) = +100\). Since the gate draws no current, the second stage does not load the first at low frequency.
